notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: All road coverage is low-quality brownish "shitcam", often with a big round blur; India has lots of it too.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Fairly long plates, mostly white; private vehicles use red and public vehicles use black.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Script with a line across the top of each word; the letter ङ is common, and native-script numerals on signs are often seen, which is rare in India.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: A concrete pole with a trident top and triangle supports is unique here; so is a square concrete pole with two widely spaced side insulators.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Square concrete poles on the flat south, thin metal poles in the mountains; tops are often tridents.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow dashed or solid edge lines with dashed white centre lines on bigger roads; solid yellow edges are common in the east of the central province.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Black-and-white striped concrete bollards, 3 to 5 stripes, often with a red mark on top.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Flat farmland in the far south, with very high mountain roads across the centre and north.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Colourful blocky multi-storey buildings or small painted-concrete, red-brick or thatched-looking houses, often with triangular facade decorations.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Black-and-white striped signposts; India, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Malaysia have them too.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: White-painted Buddhist stupas, sometimes with painted eyes on the sides, are found only here.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The western hills are dry with a lot of bare hillside.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Smooth-crowned pines with long needles grow in the mountains, more in the west and near the capital; the east is greener.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Tall narrow-crowned Japanese cedars and tea plantations are only in the far east.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Far-east roofs are sheet metal with a triangular window under the ridge and a sloping section below.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Round clay roof tiles are most common on the flat south; grey square stone tiles around Birgunj and Janakpur.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Mosques cluster in a few Muslim-majority spots in the south, such as Janakpur, Birgunj and Biratnagar.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Water tanks are mostly green or black; yellow ones are mainly in the east.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Orange cars appear around Biratnagar, Birtamod and a few western and central towns; blue cars around Pokhara and Birgunj.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Trekker coverage is only in the northeast, southwest of Mount Everest, with forest in the south and barren mountain trails in the north.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: The biggest trekker settlement by far is Namche Bazar; Khumjung has nearly all houses with green roofs.
